notes: This leaf is manuscript page 9, with a separate thin foliation 27. The main writing and the marginal additions are dark pen writing; the thinner foliation is recorded without attributing it to a particular writer.

The top continuation describes E_J intersect T as conical in T and describes a product by I^J of a conical structure on (T_J,Y_J), with dot T_J as the boundary part of the cone on Y_J. These are reported claims, not independently proved here.

Section 6 introduces stratifications indexed by a finite ordered set through an increasing family of closed subspaces X_i. The written precylindrical conditions concern successive inclusions, transverse boundary parts, and an interval identified in reverse order with a power set. The margins discuss restricting b) to maximal j and compatibility of Inf with intersections. No stratification theorem or construction is verified in this return.

The inserted word is literally minimaux, indicated by two raised i dots. This is in tension with the usual terminology for immediate predecessors of a greatest element, which would be maximal proper elements. The mathematical expectation was not substituted for the ink. A separate root check can assess the terminology; this reader performed no proof check.

The formula j >= s_k is visibly written, while the neighboring text calls s_k a part of S and the possible subscript in j in S_k remains uncertain. The reading is preserved without changing the condition to a mathematically expected formula. Likewise la parties/partie and parties bordantes transversaux are not grammatically repaired.
The first line ends at the paper edge with côniq. Neither ue nor a truncation hyphen is supplied. The top paragraph ends with four points, encoded as \ldots. rather than a three-point ellipsis.

The right-margin vertical strokes are cancelled text with a shorter cancelled addition above the main run. The above-line addition is encoded separately as inserted and deleted. No genuine diagram or free-standing drawing was found; the other large crossing strokes are insertion leaders, letter descenders, or cancellations.

The NB note is secure through maximal; its last dans I and stop remain bounded as a doubt because the rotated crop is crowded at that edge. No terminal stop is supplied after the first marginal transversaux.

Line count 28 counts the distinct main and interlinear baselines, including the isolated cancelled section numeral, the cancelled universal expression, both inserted b) lines, and the i.e. inserted explanation. Marginal lines, foliation, and small above-line word replacements are inventoried separately.

The whole image and both native halves were read before targeted crops. Thirty-one first-reading crops were produced and inspected, including one additional page-number crop. All C doubt occurrences, including struck ones, are represented in marks. No OCR, external text source, or TeX compilation was used.

In the lower-left margin, the base correspond- is readable but the ending is compressed; correspond\unsure{ent} retains a narrow doubt. H's uncertainty on the otherwise same word ordonné and its font macro for P are not counted as substantive disagreements.
